title: Fresh install renders blank frames with @react-three/postprocessing ≥ 3.0.5 (plus Windows-only script paths)
body:
## Summary
On a fresh install (macOS, Apple Silicon) `BridgeShort` renders and exits 0, but every frame is a flat `#cfe3f2`: the `AbsoluteFill` background with nothing drawn on top. No error or warning is logged.

## Cause
npm currently resolves `@react-three/postprocessing` to 3.2.x. Since **3.0.5**, `EffectComposer` builds its composer inside `useEffect` and stores it with `setState`. Remotion's `ThreeCanvas` renders with `frameloop="never"` and calls `advance()` once per frame. At that moment the composer state is still `null`, so the composer's `useFrame` returns early. Because that `useFrame` subscribes with priority 1, R3F also skips its own render, and the canvas stays transparent.

In 3.0.4 the composer is built synchronously (`useMemo`), so the first `advance()` already draws through it.

How I isolated it:
- A minimal `ThreeCanvas` with a box renders fine.
- `BridgeShort` with every post toggle off is still blank (the tone-mapping effect keeps the composer mounted).
- The same world without `EffectComposer` renders.
- With `@react-three/postprocessing@3.0.4`, the full post chain renders (ink, lens blur, bloom, grade).

## Workaround
Pin `@react-three/postprocessing@3.0.4`. Its types reject `null` children, so `Bridge.tsx` needs the composer children wrapped in one fragment. Rendered stills are byte-identical with and without the fragment.

A proper fix that also works with ≥ 3.0.5 would hold a `delayRender` until the composer exists and then advance once more. I haven't tried that.

## Other fresh-install snags
- `templates/scripts/bridge-stills.mjs` hardcodes `C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe`, and redirects only `TEMP`/`TMP`, which macOS and Linux ignore (they read `TMPDIR`).
- `templates/scripts/bridge-stills.mjs` hardcodes the `BridgeShort` composition id, although SKILL.md step 4 has you register and rename a new composition.
- `templates/scripts/bridge_merge.py` has `ROOT = os.path.expanduser("your Remotion project")`.
- The README doesn't list the 26 Kenney models that `world.ts` loads from `public/bridge/kenney/`. `loadKit()` skips missing ones silently, so the trees and stalls just vanish. The Fantasy Town Kit models also need `Textures/colormap.png`.

## Environment
macOS (Apple Silicon), Node 26.0.0, remotion / @remotion/three 4.0.541, three 0.187.0, @react-three/fiber 9.8.2, postprocessing 6.39.6, Remotion's Chrome Headless Shell (`--gl=angle`).
